My husband says he can't reason with me anymore and has been sleeping in the guest room because of all the tension.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me how long these episodes of increased energy and mood swings have been happening, and how often they occur?\n\nPatient: This intense, high-energy state has been building and staying constant for about two months now, ever since I started taking on extra shifts and managing my parents' care. I've had times in the past where I felt like my normal, calmer self, but this specific stretch has been going on non-stop.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of depression or significant low mood in the past, and if so, did they occur before, after, or at the same time as these episodes of increased energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced periods of deep depression or low mood in the past. When I'm not in this high-energy state, I usually just feel like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've had any episodes in the past where you felt extremely low or depressed that lasted for at least two weeks, or if these high-energy episodes have ever switched to a low-energy state within a short period, such as a few days or weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever having periods of feeling extremely low or depressed for weeks, and I've never experienced rapid switches to a low-energy state. Usually, I just feel like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of significantly depressed mood or loss of interest in activities that lasted for more than two weeks at any point in your life, even if it wasn't recently?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced prolonged periods of depression or lost interest in things. In the past, I have always either felt like my normal, calm self, or highly active and driven like I do now.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, which is distinct from your current high-energy state?\n\nPatient: I don't really recall ever having a period like that. Right now, I just feel way too sped up and busy with all my responsibilities to even think about the past.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, separate from your current high-energy state, or if these high-energy episodes have ever occurred in a clear pattern, such as seasonal variations or following a specific life event?\n\nPatient: I don't really remember ever having a two-week period of feeling depressed or losing interest in things, as I'm usually either my normal self or very busy. This current high-energy state definitely started with the stress of my parents' health and all my extra work shifts, but I'm not sure about any past patterns or seasonal changes.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific event, situation, or time of year that might trigger these episodes of high energy and mood swings, or do they seem to occur randomly?\n\nPatient: This current episode was definitely triggered by a lot of intense stress and overwork over the last couple of months. I had to pick up extra shifts at the care facility due to staffing shortages while also coordinating appointments and translating for my aging parents, especially after my parent had a minor stroke. It just felt like everything piled up at once and I couldn't stop.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, which is distinct from your current high-energy state, and if so, did these episodes of depression occur before, after, or at the same time as your episodes of high energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: I really don't recall ever having a period where I felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in things for two weeks. In the past, before this high-energy state started, I mostly just felt normal and calm.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if you've had any previous episodes similar to this two-month high-energy state, or if this is the first time you've experienced something like this, to help me understand if this is a recurring pattern or a one-time event?\n\nPatient: This is the absolute first time I’ve ever experienced an intense, high-energy state like this—it’s completely new to me! In the past, I had a very structured, quiet routine with early-morning tai chi, careful budgeting, and peaceful evenings where I felt like my normal, calmer self. But now, my mind is just racing and I feel this constant, breathless push to keep going and going!\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where you've experienced a sudden shift from your high-energy state to feeling somewhat calmer or more subdued, even if it was brief, to help me better understand the nature of these episodes?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any shifts to a calmer state lately at all. For the past two months, this high-energy, overcharged feeling has been completely constant and intense without any breaks. While I used to be much calmer in the past before all of this started, right now I feel completely unable to slow down.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any previous episodes of high energy that lasted less than two months, or is this current episode the only one of its kind that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: This current episode is the only one of its kind I have ever experienced. In the past, I always felt like my normal, calmer self and never had any high-energy episodes like this before.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any episodes of significantly depressed mood or loss of interest that lasted for more than two weeks, which would be distinct from your current high-energy state, to help clarify the diagnosis?\n\nPatient: I don't recall ever having a period of two weeks or more where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things. Before this high-energy state, I generally just felt like my normal, calm self.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many episodes of high energy and mood swings you've had in the past year, and if they've been getting longer or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about the exact number of episodes in the past year or if they've been getting longer, since this is the first time I've ever felt this way. This current episode has just been incredibly intense and continuous over the last two months without any breaks. One minute I'm overly cheerful and telling everyone how amazing I am at keeping everyone safe, and the next I'm snapping at my husband or coworkers because it feels like they are getting in the way of urgent tasks.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or required hospitalization due to these episodes of increased energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: Yes, it has caused terrible problems—my husband and my charge nurse actually brought me to the emergency department after I was written up at work for arguing with doctors and trying to override their orders. My husband says he can't reason with me anymore and has been sleeping in the guest room because of all the tension.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me how long these episodes of increased energy and mood swings have been happening, and how often they occur?\n\nPatient: This intense, high-energy state has been building and staying constant for about two months now, ever since I started taking on extra shifts and managing my parents' care. I've had times in the past where I felt like my normal, calmer self, but this specific stretch has been going on non-stop.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of depression or significant low mood in the past, and if so, did they occur before, after, or at the same time as these episodes of increased energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced periods of deep depression or low mood in the past. When I'm not in this high-energy state, I usually just feel like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've had any episodes in the past where you felt extremely low or depressed that lasted for at least two weeks, or if these high-energy episodes have ever switched to a low-energy state within a short period, such as a few days or weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever having periods of feeling extremely low or depressed for weeks, and I've never experienced rapid switches to a low-energy state. When these high-energy times pass, I usually just return to my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your high-energy state suddenly shifted to feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or vice versa, within a short period of time, such as a few days or weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced sudden shifts to feeling sad, empty, or hopeless like that. My main struggle right now is just that I can't slow down from this high-energy state.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted less than four days, or is this current episode the longest you've experienced?\n\nPatient: This current episode is definitely the longest and most intense thing I have ever experienced, lasting about two months now. I don't recall ever having short, minor bursts of high energy or irritability that lasted just a few days in the past. Usually, I just feel like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of significantly depressed mood or loss of interest in activities that lasted for more than two weeks at any point in your life, even if it wasn't recently?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced prolonged periods of depression or lost interest in things. In the past, I have always either felt like my normal, calm self, or highly active and driven like I do now.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, which is distinct from your current high-energy state?\n\nPatient: I don't really recall ever having a period like that. Right now, I just feel way too sped up and busy with all my responsibilities to even think about the past.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, separate from your current high-energy state, or if these high-energy episodes have ever occurred in a clear pattern, such as seasonal variations or following a specific life event?\n\nPatient: I don't really remember ever having a two-week period of feeling depressed or losing interest in things, as I'm usually either my normal self or very busy. This current high-energy state definitely started with the stress of my parents' health and all my extra work shifts, but I'm not sure about any past patterns or seasonal changes.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific event, situation, or time of year that might trigger these episodes of high energy and mood swings, or do they seem to occur randomly?\n\nPatient: This current episode was definitely triggered by a lot of intense stress and overwork over the last couple of months. I had to pick up extra shifts at the care facility due to staffing shortages while also coordinating appointments and translating for my aging parents, especially after my parent had a minor stroke. It just felt like everything piled up at once and I couldn't stop.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in activities, which is distinct from your current high-energy state, and if so, did these episodes of depression occur before, after, or at the same time as your episodes of high energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: I really don't recall ever having a period where I felt abnormally depressed or lost interest in things for two weeks. In the past, before this high-energy state started, I mostly just felt normal and calm.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if you've had any previous episodes similar to this two-month high-energy state, or if this is the first time you've experienced something like this, to help me understand if this is a recurring pattern or a one-time event?\n\nPatient: This is the absolute first time I’ve ever experienced an intense, high-energy state like this—it’s completely new to me! In the past, I had a very structured, quiet routine with early-morning tai chi, careful budgeting, and peaceful evenings where I felt like my normal, calmer self. But now, my mind is just racing and I feel this constant, breathless push to keep going and going!\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where you've experienced a sudden shift from your high-energy state to feeling somewhat calmer or more subdued, even if it was brief, to help me better understand the nature of these episodes?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any shifts to a calmer state lately at all. For the past two months, this high-energy, overcharged feeling has been completely constant and intense without any breaks. While I used to be much calmer in the past before all of this started, right now I feel completely unable to slow down.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any previous episodes of high energy that lasted less than two months, or is this current episode the only one of its kind that you've experienced?\n\nPatient: This current episode is the only one of its kind I have ever experienced. In the past, I always felt like my normal, calmer self and never had any high-energy episodes like this before.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any episodes of significantly depressed mood or loss of interest that lasted for more than two weeks, which would be distinct from your current high-energy state, to help clarify the diagnosis?\n\nPatient: I don't recall ever having a period of two weeks or more where I felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things. Before this high-energy state, I generally just felt like my normal, calm self.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many episodes of high energy and mood swings you've had in the past year, and if they've been getting longer or more frequent over time?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about the exact number of episodes in the past year or if they've been getting longer, since this is the first time I've ever felt this way. This current episode has just been incredibly intense and continuous over the last two months without any breaks. I've just been stuck in this high-energy state day and night, and it feels like it isn't stopping.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is the first time you've experienced such a prolonged high-energy state, but can you think of any shorter periods in the past where you might have felt similarly elevated or irritable, even if they didn't last as long as two months?\n\nPatient: No, I really can't think of any times like that in my past. Before this started a couple of months ago, I always just felt like my normal, calmer self. I've never experienced these kinds of intense, high-energy, or irritable periods before now.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if you have experienced any periods where your high-energy state lasted less than two months but more than a few days, to help differentiate between possible conditions?\n\nPatient: I don't recall having any other shorter periods of high energy like this in the past. Before this current two-month episode, I generally just felt like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during these episodes of high energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: Yes, but those experiences only started since I got so revved up and stopped sleeping a couple of months ago. I keep hearing a man's voice right behind my ear whispering, \"Don't sleep, they're counting on you,\" and I am completely convinced that if I'm not watching every single chart and pill, my parents and patients will die. I've never had any experiences like that when I'm feeling like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about when these psychotic symptoms, such as the voice you hear, started in relation to your high-energy state, and have they been constant or do they come and go?\n\nPatient: The voice and those intense beliefs only started about two months ago when I got really revved up and stopped needing rest, and they only happen when I'm in this high-energy state. I hear a man's voice right behind my ear telling me not to sleep because they are counting on me, especially when I'm walking down the hallway at work or trying to lie down at home. I've never experienced anything like this when I'm feeling like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other psychotic symptoms besides the voice, such as seeing things that aren't there or having delusional thoughts about your identity or purpose, during these episodes of high energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: I haven't seen things that aren't there, but I do have an unshakeable belief about my purpose right now. I am completely convinced that only I can prevent a major disaster and save my patients and parents from dying. I feel in my gut that if I am not watching every single chart and pill, the doctors and nurses will miss something fatal, even though everyone tells me everything is fine.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any disorganized thinking or speech, such as rapid switching between ideas or difficulty expressing yourself clearly, during these episodes of high energy and mood swings?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mind is racing so fast that I'll skip from thinking about my mom's blood pressure to reorganizing the med cart or the night shift schedule before I can even finish a thought. My husband and coworkers keep telling me I talk a mile a minute and jump around, but I feel like all these important thoughts will explode out of my head if I pause for even a second.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about being the only one who can prevent a disaster and save your patients and parents have affected your behavior and interactions with others during this high-energy state?\n\nPatient: Because I felt solely responsible for keeping everyone safe, I took matters into my own hands by micromanaging everything, rewriting care plans, and refusing to leave work. The voice and those intense beliefs only started when I got so revved up and stopped needing rest a couple of months ago. Whenever I've felt like my normal, calmer self in the past, I have never had those experiences.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if the psychotic symptoms, such as the voice and delusional thoughts, have been present throughout the entire two-month period of your high-energy state, or have they waxed and waned in intensity?\n\nPatient: Yes, the voice and those intense beliefs started right when I got revved up and stopped sleeping about two months ago. I've never had any experiences like this in the past when I was feeling like my normal, calmer self.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where the psychotic symptoms, such as the voice or delusional thoughts, occurred without any high-energy state or mood swings in the past, even if it was just for a brief time?"
